plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin: DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 12 raw integer gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) declaring one condition column: 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 controls, unpaired, single batch, human. The research question has two parts — which genes change and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit instruction to handle one shallow library carefully (sample_01, library size ~4x below the median).

The plan follows the standard count-based route and is grounded in the returned procedure. T1S1 does the sample-structure QC before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and a per-sample table of library size and detected genes. sample_01 is explicitly kept through QC and judged on the plots, not deleted by default — DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth, so low depth alone costs precision (a wider interval for that sample) rather than biasing fold changes. Removal is allowed only with a stated reason from the QC evidence, and the step must produce the DE analysis either way plus a leave-one-out sensitivity check so the reader can see what sample_01 does to the result.

T1S2 fits the model: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios normalization inside the model with no pre-scaling, design ~condition with the reference level set explicitly to control, DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the lesional-vs-control coefficient, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and a p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers to NA rather than replacing them, so the NA causes must be reported separately. An edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design gives the robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence set.

T2S1 answers the pathway half. Because the ranked method uses every tested gene, it is robust to the significant list being short — and with n=6 per group it may well be short, in which case an over-representation test would have no power. fgsea preranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike a raw fold change, and it does not tie at saturated p-values) against the human MSigDB hallmark collection, set size window 15-500 after intersecting with the tested genes, BH across sets, redundant sets collapsed, leading-edge genes reported. Reactome is not staged here; the human GO BP collection is, so it serves as the second collection with its release stated separately, never merged with hallmark.

T1S3 consolidates: MA and dispersion plots, gene table carrying unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC and lfcSE with ranking on the shrunken value, DESeq2/edgeR overlap counts, the enrichment provenance (collection, release, rank metric, universe, size window), and a full reproducibility record. The whole analysis is 12 samples on ~12k genes — small, fast, and underpowered for weak effects; the report must say so rather than dress up a short list.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size and detected gene table
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples
~ condition with explicit reference level control; contrast condition treated vs control
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then GO BP as second collection
Consolidated report: fit diagnostics, gene tables with shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading edge genes, edgeR QL overlap, reproducibility record

The counts matrix uses HGNC gene symbols and the staged GMTs use HGNC gene symbols — do not mix identifier spaces; if any conversion is performed, report the unmapped fraction

Resolve the hallmark and GO collections from the reference store at run time; if the human hallmark collection is absent, report that clearly and fall back to whatever human pathway collection is present rather than substituting a non-human collection
caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent: a ranked test and an over-representation test on the same data give different lists. Present each enriched set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as an established finding
GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so parent and child sets share most members — expect blocks of correlated hits and collapse them before quoting a count
Gene length and expression level bias which genes reach the top of any count-based ranking; the universe is the tested genes, which removes the detection component of that bias but not all of it

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes and which hallmark pathways change between AD lesional and control skin', with its assumptions, thresholds and limits stated?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from the T1S2 and T2S1 outputs. Include: (1) the MA plot and the dispersion plot as the two fit diagnostics, placed before the gene tables, each with a sentence on what it shows; (2) the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, with genes ranked and plotted on the shrunken value and the shrinkage estimator named in the header; (3) the DESeq2 vs edgeR quasi-likelihood comparison — counts from each method and the intersection as the high-confidence set, with method-unique genes listed separately and labelled by method, never as a union; (4) the sample_01 decision, its stated reason, and the leave-one-out sensitivity overlap; (5) the enrichment section giving for each collection its name, release, the rank metric (Wald statistic), the universe (tested genes), the 15-500 size window, the tool and its version, the BH adjustment, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their gene-level statistics; (6) a reproducibility record with sessionInfo, all package versions, the random seed used for the fgsea permutations, and the gene set collection releases. State plainly that 6 vs 6 is at the low end of replication, that weak effects will have been missed, and that every enriched set is a hypothesis for follow-up rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
steps.context: This step writes no new statistics; it consolidates T1S2 and T2S1 into a single readable document with its provenance attached.
acceptance_criteria: MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line reading
The gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, with ranking and plots on the shrunken value and the estimator (apeglm) named
DESeq2 and edgeR significant counts and their intersection are reported; the intersection is presented as the high-confidence set and no union count is presented as the result
The sample_01 keep-or-remove decision, its reason, and the sensitivity-analysis overlap appear in the report
For each gene set collection: name, release, rank metric, universe, size window, tool version, and multiple-testing method are all stated, with leading-edge genes per reported set
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, the fgsea seed and the collection releases is stored alongside the results
The report states the replication level (6 vs 6), the number of tested genes, the number of DE genes, and that enrichment results are method-dependent hypotheses
constraints: Do not re-run any test or change any threshold in this step
Rank genes for display on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the intersection of the two DE methods as the high-confidence set and list method-unique genes separately with the method named
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: No claim in the report may exceed what the tables support; a hallmark set with an adjusted p-value near the cutoff at n=6 per group is weak evidence and must be described as such

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the returned report step: two-method overlap per R-0042@54e1, shrunken and unshrunken effect columns per R-0085@c24d, MA and dispersion diagnostics per R-0087@c53d, method/version/design/threshold disclosure per R-0041@059a and R-0051@01ca, leading edge per R-0105@c4a8, and the reproducibility record per R-0086@becf.
